Coalesce

koh-uh-LESS · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To coalesce is to come together and form one mass.

Over the course of the meeting, a dozen scattered proposals slowly began to coalesce into one clear plan.

Worked Example

The scattered protest groups eventually coalesced into a single, well-organized movement with shared leadership.

Separate groups merging over time into one unified whole is exactly the process coalesce describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

merge: combine to form a single entity

converge: come together from different directions

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

disperse: spread out or scatter

fragment: break into smaller pieces

Where it sits · how tightly things join into one — combine → coalesce → fuse

combine vs. coalesce: To combine things is simply to join them; to coalesce is for many separate, scattered things to gradually grow into one unified whole.

fuse vs. coalesce: Fuse suggests an even tighter, often permanent joining than coalesce, sometimes implying heat or pressure rather than gradual growth.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — co-

prefix — co-: together (Latin (com-))

root — alesc

root — alesc: to grow up (Latin (alescere))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Co- ('together') plus alesc- ('to grow up,' from alescere) plus the verb-forming -e gives 'to grow up together' -- coalescing means separate parts developing into one unified whole.

Use the root in a new word: adolescent

Use the root in a new word: adolescent: Adolescent shares the same alescere root as coalesce -- one describes a person growing up, the other describes separate parts 'growing together' into one.

Root Check

Word Choice

Coalesce implies a genuinely unified whole forming from separate parts -- not just an agreement or partnership between things that stay separate. When separation is only partly overcome, 'merge' or 'combine' often fits more precisely.
